Base

O

desses

sanguínea

(BSI)

por

esses

em

tem

Avaliar

a

mortalidade

em

30

dias

para

os

mediadores

do

desfecho.

:

de

coorte

realizado

em

três

pacientes

de

18

com

BSI

por

Enterobacterales
.

nos

WHO

1

de

geração

e

carbapenêmicos),

WHO

2

(3GCR)

e

WHO

3

(CRE).

Um

modelo

de

Cox

avaliou

os

efeitos

mediadores

da

gravidade

e

da

terapia

sobre

a

mortalidade.

ABSTRACT


Background
:

Third-generation

cephalosporin-resistant

(3GCR)

and

carbapenem-resistant

(CRE)

Enterobacterales

are

critical

priority

resistance

profiles

according

to

WHO.

The

impact

of

these

profiles

in

bloodstream

infections

(BSI)

caused

by

these

pathogens

in

pediatric

has

been

scarcely

investigated.


Objective:

Evaluate

30-day

mortality

and

utilize

hierarchical

modeling

to

evaluate

mediators

of

the

outcome.


Methods
:

A

multicenter

retrospective

cohort

study

in

three

Brazilian

tertiary

hospitals

(2018–2023)

included

patients

<18

years

with

Enterobacterales

BSI.

Isolates

were

stratified

into

WHO

profile

1

(3GC

and

carbapenem-susceptible),

2

(3GCR),

and

3

(CRE).

A

hierarchical

Cox

model

assessed

mediating

effects

of

severity

and

therapy

on

mortality.


Results
:

Of

264

patients,

165

(62.5%)

were

WHO

1,

75

(28.4%)

WHO

2,

and

24

(9.1%)

WHO

3.

Crude

mortality

was

9.1%,

13.3%,

and

33.3%,

respectively

(P

=

0.003).

The

unadjusted

HR

for

WHO

2

and

3

compared

to

WHO

1

was

1.52

(95%

CI

0.68–3.39)

and

4.09

(95%

CI

1.74–9.60),

respectively.

Adjusted

for

baseline

characteristics

(demographics

and

comorbidities),

WHO

3

was

significantly

associated

with

death

(aHR

3.00;

95%

CI

1.26–7.13).

Adding

variables

associated

with

severity

of

the

BSI

episodes

attenuated

this

association

of

WHO

3

(aHR

2.205;

95%

CI

0.910−5.347).

In

the

final

model

including

variables

associated

with

antimicrobial

therapy,

WHO

3

was

no

longer

associated

with

mortality

(HR

0.81;

95%

CI

0.31–2.16).

WHO

2

was

not

significantly

associated

with

mortality

in

any

of

the

above

steps.


Conclusion
:

Our

study

suggests

that

the

increased

mortality

of

CRE

BSI

in

pediatric

is

majorly

determined

by

difficulties

in

instituting

adequate

therapy,

but

the

clinical

severity

of

patients

have

also

mediated

this

effect.

Timely

effective

antimicrobial

therapy

remains

the

primary

modifiable

factor.

INTRODUÇÃO

A

resistência

antimicrobiana

(do

inglês

antimicrobial

resistance,

AMR)

emergiu

como

uma

das

maiores

ameaças

à

saúde

pública

do

século

XXI.
1

Estimativas

globais

indicam

que,

em

2021,

a

AMR

esteve

associada

a

mais

de

um

milhão

de

mortes,

com

projeções

que

apontam

para

um

aumento

progressivo

desse

impacto,

podendo

ultrapassar

1,9

milhão

de

óbitos

anuais

até

2050,

caso

estratégias

efetivas

de

contenção

não

sejam

implementadas.
1


Nesse

contexto,

a

Organização

Mundial

da

Saúde

(WHO)

estabeleceu

uma

lista

de

patógenos

prioritários,

originalmente

proposta

em

2017

e

atualizada

em

2024,

na

qual

a

ordem

Enterobacterales

permanece

em

posição

de

destaque,

com

os

fenótipos

resistentes

a

cefalosporinas

de

terceira

geração

(3GCR)

e

a

carbapenêmicos

(CRE)

classificados

como

prioridade

crítica.
2

Na

população

pediátrica,

a

incidência

dessas

infecções

relacionadas

à

assistência

à

saúde

tem

crescido,

impondo

desafios

clínicos

substanciais.
3,4

Dados

da

literatura

apontam

que

a

mortalidade

em

30

dias

é

alta,

variando

de

37%

em

neonatos

e

lactentes

com

infecções

por

3GCR

até

52%

em

crianças

com

BSI

por

CRE.
5,6

Apesar

desses

índices

alarmante,

a

literatura

vigente

tende

a

atribuir

essa

mortalidade

predominantemente

à

gravidade

clínica

basal,

frequentemente

subestimando

o

papel

da

dificuldade

de

manejo

terapêutico

como

um

mecanismo

causal

distinto.
6–8

Até

o

momento,

desconhecemos

outro

estudo

em

doenças

infecciosas

pediátricas

que

tenha

explorado

essa

associação

específica

por

meio

de

análise

de

mediação.

Enquanto

modelos

convencionais

tratam

a

terapia

e

a

gravidade

como

variáveis

concorrentes,

falhando

em

capturar

a

cadeia

causal,

a

análise

hierárquica

permite

testar

a

hipótese

de

que

a

inadequação

terapêutica

possa

atuar

como

mediador

do

desfecho,

explicando

a

associação

observada

entre

resistência

e

morte

independentemente

da

gravidade

clínica

basal.
7–9

este

estudo

teve

como

objetivo

ABSTRACT


Background
:

Third-generation

cephalosporin-resistant

(3GCR)

and

carbapenem-resistant

(CRE)

Enterobacterales

are

critical

priority

resistance

profiles

according

to

WHO.

The

impact

of

these

profiles

in

bloodstream

infections

(BSI)

caused

by

these

pathogens

in

pediatric

has

been

scarcely

investigated.


Objective:

Evaluate

30-day

mortality

and

utilize

hierarchical

modeling

to

evaluate

mediators

of

the

outcome.


Methods
:

A

multicenter

retrospective

cohort

study

in

three

Brazilian

tertiary

hospitals

(2018–2023)

included

patients

<18

years

with

Enterobacterales

BSI.

Isolates

were

stratified

into

WHO

profile

1

(3GC

and

carbapenem-susceptible),

2

(3GCR),

and

3

(CRE).

A

hierarchical

Cox

model

assessed

mediating

effects

of

severity

and

therapy

on

mortality.


Results
:

Of

264

patients,

165

(62.5%)

were

WHO

1,

75

(28.4%)

WHO

2,

and

24

(9.1%)

WHO

3.

Crude

mortality

was

9.1%,

13.3%,

and

33.3%,

respectively

(P

=

0.003).

The

unadjusted

HR

for

WHO

2

and

3

compared

to

WHO

1

was

1.52

(95%

CI

0.68–3.39)

and

4.09

(95%

CI

1.74–9.60),

respectively.

Adjusted

for

baseline

characteristics

(demographics

and

comorbidities),

WHO

3

was

significantly

associated

with

death

(aHR

3.00;

95%

CI

1.26–7.13).

Adding

variables

associated

with

severity

of

the

BSI

episodes

attenuated

this

association

of

WHO

3

(aHR

2.205;

95%

CI

0.910−5.347).

In

the

final

model

including

variables

associated

with

antimicrobial

therapy,

WHO

3

was

no

longer

associated

with

mortality

(HR

0.81;

95%

CI

0.31–2.16).

WHO

2

was

not

significantly

associated

with

mortality

in

any

of

the

above

steps.


Conclusion
:

Our

study

suggests

that

the

increased

mortality

of

CRE

BSI

in

pediatric

is

majorly

determined

by

difficulties

in

instituting

adequate

therapy,

but

the

clinical

severity

of

patients

have

also

mediated

this

effect.

Timely

effective

antimicrobial

therapy

remains

the

primary

modifiable

factor.
